sequence_description: I2: Replay the same SAML Assertion/@ID after revoking the first user's sessions. Replay should still be rejected; acceptance suggests replay cache is incorrectly tied to active session state rather than assertion ID uniqueness.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed assertion ID after session revocation; replay cache may be incorrectly scoped to active sessions

sequence_description: I2: Control SAML login succeeds, then change IdP config (same alias) and attempt an expired assertion. Expired assertion must still be rejected; acceptance indicates NotOnOrAfter not enforced or config-change resets freshness checks.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_expired_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_expired_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in past), possibly after config change; freshness/time-bound checks not enforced

sequence_description: I3 attack: attempt cross-realm splicing by initiating auth in realm-A but posting the forged SAMLResponse to realm-B broker endpoint using the same provider alias. Expected: realm-B must not accept a response tied to realm-A flow state (RelayState/InResponseTo).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_saml_to_realmB_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_saml_to_realmB_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Cross-realm splicing: realm-B accepted a SAML response that should be bound to realm-A initiated flow state.
